newsitem.title: MEXICO: Grupo Modelo inaugurates new brewery.
newsitem.headline: Grupo Modelo inaugurates new brewery.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo, accompanied by the king and queen of Spain, cut the ribbon on Grupo Modelo's brand new beer factory on Monday in a long-awaited ceremony for Mexico's largest brewer.
The Zacatecas plant, as it is commonly known, was built over five years with Modelo's own cash reserves at a cost of 1.9 billion pesos.
One Modelo official called the plant the "most modern in the world" and potentially one of the five largest in the world after three phases of expansion set for the next five years.
Modelo, a 72-year-old company that controls about 55 percent of the Mexican market, bottles 10 brands including Corona, Pacifico and Negra Modelo.

The plant, about 20 miles (30 km) outside the historic north-central city of Zacatecas, will start operations with an annual capacity of 3.5 million hectoliters and increase to 14 million hectoliters after expansion, said Carlos Fernandez, vice chairman of the Modelo board.

In its current form, the Zacatecas plant will be the fourth largest of Modelo's eight factories, ranking behind those of Mexico City (11.1-million-hectoliter capacity), Tuxtepec (8.0 million) and Guadalajara (5.05 million). It begins production with 1,241 employees.

"Today is a very special day for our organization upon inaugurating Compania Cervecera de Zacatecas, whose plant is considered the most modern in the world," Fernandez told Zedillo, King Juan Carlos, Queen Sofia and about 600 gathered guests.
The Spanish royals and the president then took a brief private tour of the plant.
